thesis: Wrath of God taught control decks that one card could erase an entire creature battlefield, shifting the game from individual trades to managing commitment and recovery.

competitiveTimeline.significance: The archive follows Wrath from the first championship control decks through classic U/W control, creature-heavy Standard, and later board-control strategies.

playbook.role: Delay Wrath until it gains real card advantage, but do not become so greedy that haste or protection makes it unusable. Build with planeswalkers, lands, or recursive threats that survive the reset.

counterplay.directAnswers: Commit only enough creatures to demand the sweeper, preserve haste or manlands for the next turn, and use protection, recursion, or counterspells to punish the control player's reliance on one reset.
